# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋]

I need to think about this carefully. Mute has already gestured to me at the start of this round (before my turn). I can see gestures from Mute. Blind cannot see gestures, so Blind didn't get these. Blind also goes before me in turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), so whatever Blind said in speech, I should have heard — but I don't hear anything either (I'm Deaf, can't hear speech). Wait, I never receive speech at all.

So the gestures from Mute are my only information channel from Mute. Let me interpret: [☝ 🖐] could mean "one, five" or similar counting. [✌ 👊] could mean "two, [something]". [✋ ✋] could mean "five, five" or "stop, stop".

Since I can't be sure of a shared code yet, I should report what I see on the bomb to Blind (who can act) and Mute (who has the manual), since my speech reaches both Mute and Blind.

I'll describe the board plainly in speech, and try a simple gesture back to Mute acknowledging receipt, using numbers to indicate wire count.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is green. Button is large, labeled push to defuse. Three wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute is gesturing to me again. [☝ ☝ ☝] — three "one" gestures, possibly meaning "wire 1, wire 1, wire 1" (emphasis) or "rule one" or counting to three, or asking about wire 1 specifically. Since Blind can't see gestures, this exchange is purely between Mute and me.

This could be Mute asking me to confirm something about wire 1, or indicating "the manual says something about wire number 1" repeated for emphasis, or it might mean "instruction 1" three times as confirmation.

Given the earlier gestures [☝ 🖐] (maybe "wire 1, five/stop"), [✌ 👊] (wire 2, punch/cut?), [✋ ✋] (stop, stop) — these might have been Mute trying to ask me about each wire's color one at a time, but since gestures carry no words, Mute can't ask complex questions this way easily either. More likely Mute is trying to build a numeral code with me, and now repeating ☝ three times might mean "confirm: how many wires" or "wire one - tell me about it again."

I already told them wire 1 is red. Let me reinforce with gesture since Mute can't hear... wait, Mute CAN hear my speech (Mute is not deaf to speech, just can't speak). So my speech already reached Mute. So Mute knows wire 1 is red, 2 is green, 3 is yellow from my speech. The repeated ☝☝☝ might be Mute confirming/emphasizing "wire 1" is the important one - perhaps the manual says wire 1 is the answer or the manual wants to confirm which is red.

I'll gesture back confirming wire 1 is red, using a color-indicating approach isn't possible via gesture. I'll speak plainly restating for Blind too, and gesture acknowledgment.

```
speak(text="Confirming: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. Display 0, light green, button large push to defuse.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

Mute gestured [☝ 👍] to me — likely "wire 1, yes/good" confirming that wire 1 (red) is correct/the one to cut, or acknowledging my confirmation. This seems like agreement forming: wire 1 is the target.

Since Blind cannot see gestures, and Blind needs to act, I should relay this via speech (which Blind and Mute both hear). Let me speak to Blind and Mute together, stating my belief that wire 1 (red) seems to be indicated as correct, but I should be careful — I'm inferring from gestures, not certain. Let me confirm with Mute first via gesture before telling Blind to act, since a wrong cut kills everyone.

Actually, since it's my turn and next Mute speaks (wait, order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — so after me it goes back to Mute next round). I should relay to Blind now since Blind acts after receiving info, but Blind already had their turn this round before me. My speech now will reach Blind at start of next round.

I'll speak clearly to confirm the plan, addressing both, so it's ready for Blind next round, and gesture back to Mute to confirm understanding.

```
speak(text="I believe wire 1, the red one, is confirmed as correct by Mute's gesture. Blind, if Mute agrees, cut wire 1 red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new gestures from Mute this round, meaning Mute didn't send anything new to me. Blind likely spoke this round (before me), but I can't hear speech, so I have no new info from Blind either.

Since nothing new arrived, I should just maintain my previous stance and wait, or re-confirm my read of the board in case it changed (it hasn't). I'll gesture a simple confirmation to Mute to keep the channel alive, and speak once more restating the plan clearly for Blind's benefit at the start of next round.

```
speak(text="Board unchanged: display 0, light green, wires 1 red 2 green 3 yellow, button large push to defuse. Plan stands: cut wire 1 red if Mute confirms.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🫵"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 👍]

Mute gestured [☝ 👍 👍] — this reinforces "wire 1, yes, yes" — strong confirmation that wire 1 (red) is the correct action. This seems like clear agreement building between me and Mute.

I should now clearly communicate to Blind (via speech, which Blind receives) that both Mute and I agree wire 1 should be cut. I'll also gesture back a final confirmation to Mute.

```
speak(text="Confirmed twice now by Mute's gestures: wire 1, the red wire, is correct. Blind, please cut wire 1 red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍", "👍"])
```
